deeper.title: What the price assumes
deeper.text: The price assumes about 22% a year growth in free cash flow for 10 years, then 3% (discount rate 9.9% = 10-year Treasury 4.9% + 5%; base: last 12 months of free cash flow). For comparison, sales grew 18% last year; 17%/yr over 3 years — roughly in line with its recent growth.

deeper.title: Return on capital
deeper.text: 30% (3 years ago 51%, falling) — each $100 invested in the business (debt + equity, net of cash) earns about $30 a year after tax; return on shareholders' equity 30% (3 years ago 35%).

deeper.title: Signed future revenue
deeper.text: Signed but not yet delivered (remaining performance obligations): $683.0B, up 72% from a year ago — about 2.0× the last 12 months of sales; customer prepayments not yet earned (deferred revenue): $69.6B, up 13% from a year ago.

deeper.title: Multi-year view
deeper.text: Sales grew 17%/yr over 3 years and 14%/yr over 5 years; operating margin today 47% vs a 5-year range of 41–47% (median 45%): near the top of a fairly narrow range.
deeper.margin_position: near the top of a fairly narrow range

deeper.title: Cash returned to shareholders
deeper.text: Returned $48.0B to shareholders over the last 12 months ($21.0B buybacks + $27.0B dividends) = 1.3% of the company's market value. Share count down 0.3% from a year ago (about flat).

deeper.title: Analyst estimates
deeper.text: Next year's earnings-per-share estimate $24.23, up 3% in 90 days (up 2% in the last 30); 25 analysts raised, 3 cut in 30 days. This year's earnings-per-share estimate $20.03, up 1% in 90 days (up 1% in the last 30); 25 analysts raised, 3 cut in 30 days. Source: Yahoo (unofficial).

deeper.title: Vs peers
deeper.text: Compared with 7 peers (ORCL, GOOGL, AMZN, CRM, ADBE, NOW, IBM): sales growth over the last 12 months 18% vs a median of 15%; operating margin 47% vs 26%; price/sales 10.6× vs 3.6×.

deeper.title: Where sales come from
deeper.text: By segment, latest quarter vs a year earlier: Agents and infra 83% of sales, up 25%; Devices and consumer 17% of sales, down 3%. Source: 10-Q XBRL.

deeper.title: Insider trading
deeper.text: Last 90 days: no open-market purchases; sales $74.8M, 96% under pre-set 10b5-1 trading plans. Source: SEC Form 4.

deeper.title: New risk factors
deeper.text: 4 new risk-factor headings vs last year's annual report, e.g. “Our cloud and AI strategy requires substantial investments and depends on evolving customer demand, technologi…”; “Our success depends on our ability to develop, deliver, and maintain competitive cloud-based and AI products a…”.

note.headline: Microsoft edges up to 496.13, holding above support; hold, swing trade stays on

summary.thesis: Microsoft's sales and margins are improving, but free cash flow is shrinking and the price already assumes heavy spending will pay off, so the stock looks fairly priced against its own history and expensive on cash flow.
summary.decision: Long-term: hold, and add only at 475.73. Swing: stay in yesterday's trade, with new entries at 490.27, a stop at 475.34 and a target at 511.78.
summary.act_at: Add at 475.73; swing entry 490.27, stop 475.34, target 511.78

note.happening: Microsoft closed at 496.13, up 0.74%. It stayed above the 485.58–490.27 support zone, which the price has touched 7 times, and it remains below the falling 20-day average of 518.38. There is no news since the last note, and the next earnings report is on 2027-01-27.
note.business: The business itself is getting stronger. Quarterly sales grew 18.8% from a year earlier, slightly faster than the 18.3% two quarters ago. Operating margin, the share of sales left after running costs, rose to 47.1% from 46.27%. Analysts have raised next-year earnings per share to 24.2 from 23.68 a month ago. The pressure is on cash. Trailing free cash flow, the cash left after investment, fell to 60.0B from 78.0B. The filings say each dollar invested now earns 30¢ a year, down from 51¢ three years ago, so the heavy spending is not paying back yet. The balance sheet is not at risk: net cash is 29.0B and the share count shrank 0.27% over the year. What is at risk is the return on that spending, not demand or solvency. The 4 new risk headings in the annual report and the weak tech market (the macro read is a downtrend with elevated fear) affect sentiment, not the business.

worth.text: The valuation methods disagree sharply. A cash-flow model starting from today's 60.0B of free cash flow gives 180.81 to 288.62, with a base case of 218.43. To justify 496.13 on cash flow alone, free cash flow would have to start growing at about 39.7% a year. That is far above the 17% to 21% growth rates the model uses, and even 30% growth only gives 350.1. Measured against its own past price-to-sales, the stock looks fair: 475.73 at the low end, 535.43 in the middle and 592.92 at the high end. Today's price-to-sales of 10.6 sits at the 33rd percentile of its own 5-year range. Against peers it looks expensive, at 10.6 times sales versus a peer median of 3.5. The whole gap between the methods comes down to one question: does today's depressed cash flow describe the business, or will it recover as the spending matures? This note takes the own-history range from 475.73 to 535.43 and accepts that the cash-flow model is a real warning.
worth.key_assumption: The spending that cut free cash flow from 78.0B to 60.0B turns back into cash, so next-year earnings (estimate 24.2) are the right basis for value, not today's cash flow.

bull: Sales growth is speeding up a little: 18.8% from a year earlier last quarter, against 18.3% two quarters ago.

Margins are improving: operating margin rose to 47.1% from 46.27%, and net cash is 29.0B.
bear: Free cash flow fell to 60.0B from 78.0B, and each invested dollar now earns 30¢ a year versus 51¢ three years ago.
The price implies about 39.7% starting cash-flow growth, while the cash-flow base case is 218.43 per share.

swing.why: Yesterday's trade, triggered at 491.22, is still on, and the close of 496.13 held above the 485.58–490.27 zone (7 touches). New entries are at the top of that zone. decision.timing: The 2026-12-18 options price a 7.4% move, so the swing target fits inside that window. Any swing position closes before the 2027-01-27 report, which the 2027-02-19 options price at a 13.7% move. Long-term money beyond the 475.73 add waits for that report's free cash flow figure.

change_mind: A close below 475.34 breaks both support zones and the bottom of the fair range. That would end the swing trade and stop all long-term adds until the 2027-01-27 report.
